title: Order checkout failing
executive_summary: Order checkout failures (order-service error rate ~0.6% -> ~29-32%, onset 15:23-15:25Z) coincide within about one minute of a configuration change by config-bot (OPS-2375) that cut order-service's payment_client.timeout_ms from 3000ms to 300ms at 15:22Z. Order-service logs are dominated by 'request to payment-service timed out after 300ms' errors, followed by circuit-breaker OPEN and retry-budget exhaustion. payment-service shows no degradation (p50/p95 latency, error rate and CPU flat vs baseline), consistent with the payment team's claim that their service is healthy. The timeout reduction is the most likely cause; the mechanism for why a 300ms timeout times out on a payment service whose p95 is ~150ms is not fully explained by the available data.

hypotheses.description: Config change reducing order-service payment_client.timeout_ms from 3000ms to 300ms (cfg-7f81d14a, OPS-2375) causes payment calls to time out, driving checkout failures. Mechanism: With a 300ms client timeout, a fraction of POST /v1/charges calls exceed the budget, triggering timeouts, circuit breaker opening (failure ratio 0.64) and retry-budget exhaustion, so checkout requests fail. Order-service error and timeout rates step up at 15:23-15:25Z, within ~1-3 minutes of the change at 15:22Z.

probable_root_cause.description: Config change reducing order-service payment_client.timeout_ms from 3000ms to 300ms (cfg-7f81d14a, OPS-2375) causes payment calls to time out, driving checkout failures.
probable_root_cause.label: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed)

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): configuration_regression in order-service - Config change reducing order-service payment_client.timeout_ms from 3000ms to 300ms (cfg-7f81d14a, OPS-2375) causes payment calls to time out, driving checkout failures.
corrective_actions: Revert payment_client.timeout_ms on order-service from 300ms to the previous 3000ms (cfg-7f81d14a) and confirm error rate returns to ~0.6%
Reset the payment-service circuit breaker on order-service after the revert and verify recovery of checkout
preventive_actions: Require review/validation for timeout changes on payment clients; guard config-bot changes with bounds checks (e.g., reject >10x reduction without approval)
Canary config changes to a subset of order-service instances before fleet-wide rollout
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on order-service payment_client timeout rate and circuit-breaker OPEN events
Dashboard payment-service p99 and client-side latency as seen by order-service to validate timeout budgets
limitations: Investigation relied on aggregated metrics and log patterns; individual request traces were not available
Deployment and config queries were limited to the 14:00-15:50Z window and specific keys
[agent-reported gap] payment-service tail latency (p99/p999) and client-side traces not available
[agent-reported gap] No direct trace of timed-out requests showing where the time was spent
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The checkout failure is most likely caused by the order-service payment client timeout being reduced from 3000ms to 300ms at 15:22Z (cfg-7f81d14a), which precedes the error onset at 15:23Z. Payment-service shows no degradation, so the payment team's health claim is consistent with the data. Status is PROBABLE rather than confirmed because payment tail latency and request-level traces are not available to explain why a 300ms timeout fails at this rate when payment p95 is ~150ms.
